claims.text: The alloy is a refractory high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state.
The intervention is addition of 5 at.% W to the alloy composition.
Adding 5 at.% W will increase yield strength by 25% relative to the W-free baseline at 1000°C under tensile loading.
The W-free baseline alloy has a yield strength of approximately 500 MPa at 1000°C.
W addition produces enhanced solid-solution strengthening.
W atoms create lattice distortions in the alloy.
The W-induced lattice distortions increase resistance to dislocation motion.
Increased resistance to dislocation motion enhances high-temperature yield strength.
The yield-strength improvement will persist under tensile loading at temperatures up to 1100°C.
The magnitude of the yield-strength improvement may depend on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions.
Grain size and precipitate formation may influence the proposed solid-solution-strengthening mechanism.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if the W-containing alloy's yield strength is less than 15% higher than that of the baseline at 1000°C.

contradictions.description: The quantitative hypothesis predicts a 25% increase, but the stated falsification rule would not falsify results between 15% and 25%; thus the experiment is not decisive for the stated effect size.
